headline: Underwriting and investment income both improve
summary_short: Net income rose 22.0% year-over-year to $191.6M ($5.38 diluted EPS, +25.1%) as the combined ratio improved 1.3 points to 91.2%, with catastrophe losses down and Personal Lines underwriting profit more than doubling to $69.4M from $25.2M a year ago.
summary_long: Operating income before interest and taxes rose 20.0% year-over-year to $251.9M on lower catastrophe losses ($104.7M vs $113.5M), higher net investment income ($119.6M vs $105.5M), and improved underwriting led by Personal Lines, where underwriting profit rose to $69.4M from $25.2M as homeowners and auto losses eased despite renewal price increases of roughly 11% and 7%, respectively. Core Commercial and Specialty underwriting profit both fell on higher current-accident-year losses in workers' compensation, commercial multiple peril, and Marine & Industrial Property. Net premiums written grew 4.6% to $1,656.8M on new business and renewal pricing. The board authorized a new $700M buyback (May 2026, $667M remaining) after redeeming $375M of debentures in January using 2025 debt-issuance proceeds; equity rose to $3,672.5M.

drivers.explanation: Operating income improved on lower catastrophe losses, higher net investment income, and better current-accident-year underwriting results, led by Personal Lines.
Increase was primarily due to higher after-tax operating income, which rose $30.5 million year-over-year on the same catastrophe, investment-income, and underwriting drivers.
Net premiums earned grew with net premiums written (new business plus renewal price increases), and net investment income rose to $119.6M from $105.5M.
EPS grew faster than net income (+25.1% vs +22.0%) because diluted weighted-average shares fell 2.5% year-over-year (35.6M vs 36.5M) on continued buybacks.
Driven by lower catastrophe losses, higher net investment income, and improved current-accident-year underwriting results, primarily in Personal Lines.
Personal Lines catastrophe losses fell to $55.4M from $70.2M and current-accident-year underwriting profit ex-cat rose $21.9M on lower homeowners and personal-auto losses.
Increase driven by higher new business volume and the impact of renewal price increases across segments.

Not explained in the release; the filing only discusses the broader cash-and-investments balance, which fell on debt redemption, buybacks, and dividend funding, not the standalone cash line's own move.

Reflects a January 15, 2026 redemption of $375.0M of 4.50% senior debentures funded from an August 2025 debt issuance, reclassifying debt from short-term to long-term rather than new quarterly borrowing.
